records.title: Hebrew Bible / KJV · Tabor is a named place
records.note: Judges 4, Psalm 89:12, Jeremiah 46:18 and Hosea 5:1 name Tabor in their own contexts. These are the baseline texts for testing an earlier wording or place tradition.
links: Hebrew and Aramaic Lexicon of the Old Testament · תבור

records.title: First-century Gospel accounts · unnamed mountain
records.note: Matthew 17:1–9, Mark 9:2–8 and Luke 9:28–36 recount the Transfiguration. In the KJV, Matthew explicitly describes a shining face and bright clothing. All three leave the mountain unnamed. The KJV is a 1611 translation.

records.title: KJV · Light, testimony and false appearance
records.note: John 8:12 supplies an early Christian light-of-the-world formulation independent of a Tabor place-name. John 3:21 concerns coming to the light, 2 Corinthians 4:4 the glorious gospel of Christ, and 2 Corinthians 11:14 the angel-of-light image. Compare the phrases in their own contexts.

records.title: 325 and 381 · creedal light language
records.note: Both transmitted creeds use Light of Light in their description of Christ. These lines concern the Son’s relationship to the Father. Neither creed identifies or renames Mount Tabor. This is distinct from the later Roman feast.

records.title: Mid-fourth century · Cyril names Mount Tabor
records.note: In Catechetical Lecture 12 §16 Cyril of Jerusalem explicitly places the Transfiguration at Mount Tabor. This gives a dated post-Gospel witness to the place tradition. Earlier attributions such as Origen need the exact text and edition verified.

records.title: 404 CE · Jerome records Paula’s ascent
records.note: Letter 108 describes Paula climbing Mount Tabor and associates it with the Transfiguration. Keep the 404 letter separate from Jerome’s earlier Gospel revision when tracing the transmission of wording.

records.title: Fourteenth century · an argument over the nature of the light
records.note: Gregory Palamas treats the light of Tabor as divine and uncreated. The 1341–1351 Constantinopolitan controversy involved different accounts of the light’s nature. The relevant decisions belong to Byzantine church history.

records.title: 1457 · the Roman liturgical calendar
records.note: Vatican News dates Pope Callixtus III’s inclusion of the feast in the Roman calendar to 1457 in connection with the victory at Belgrade the previous year. It also names Mount Tabor. This is a concrete change in Roman liturgical practice.
links: Vatican News · 1457 inclusion in the Roman calendar

records.title: 2002–2011 · Catholic use of both the place and Christ-centered framing
records.note: John Paul II in 2002 and Benedict XVI in March 2006 explicitly name Tabor and identify the event with Christ. Benedict’s August 2006 and March 2011 statements emphasize the light as divine glory or God’s light. Compare the published texts for co-use and differences in emphasis.

records.title: “Tabor Light being rotated to fake light aka Christ Light”
records.note: Nathan Tabor’s thesis asks who shifted the label, when, in which text, and with what effect. The dated record supports changes in wording and liturgical framing. It contains explicit co-use of Tabor and Christ language in Catholic sources. No primary document located in this pass establishes a deliberate Vatican renaming or the appropriation of an earlier non-Christian doctrine called Tabor Light.

records.title: What would establish the proposed rotation?
records.note: Find an independently dated earlier source using the supposed original term and meaning. Compare the same passage across verifiable witnesses in Greek, Latin or another source language. Identify the institutional actor and a dated directive, revision or contemporary report. Code place-name loss, theological reframing and intentional replacement as separate claims.
